title: dedicated: add burst token-bucket autoscaler + enhanced fleet utilization reporting
author: Diego Martinez
description:
Motivation: customers on Dedicated fleets have been hitting short, high-throughput bursts that cause sustained latency/regret when autoscalers scale only by steady-state util. This PR introduces a token-bucket style burst policy for the Dedicated fleet autoscaler and improves utilization reporting so SRE and customers can reason about burst consumption and throughput guarantees.

What changed: implemented a burst_token_bucket autoscaling policy that maintains a burst credit balance per-fleet and permits short-term scaling above steady target up to a configured token budget. Added a new config block in fleet.spec.autoscaling.burst with fields: max_burst_replicas, refill_rate_rps, token_cost_per_replica, and burst_cooldown. Autoscaler now tracks token balance with an efficient sliding-window counter and prefers draining cached burst tokens before triggering global scale-up to reduce churn.

Observability: new metrics: dedicated_fleet_burst_tokens{fleet}, dedicated_fleet_burst_consumption_rps, dedicated_fleet_burst_replenish_rate, dedicated_fleet_apparent_throughput and enhanced labels for per-route utilization. Telemetry emitted to the observability pipeline and surfaced in Redwood Console under the Dedicated -> Fleet -> Burst tab.

Compatibility/migration: default behavior is unchanged (burst policy disabled). Fleet CRD version bumped (v1alpha6 -> v1alpha7) to add the burst block and reporting fields. We provide a migration helper that backfills default burst configs for existing fleets and a feature flag (autoscaler.burst.enable) so operators can opt-in.

Testing: unit tests for token accounting, e2e integration in perf-canary cluster that validates a 30s burst above steady capacity without SLA violations, and load tests that compare cost and latency with and without burst policy.

Files of note: autoscaler/core/burst_tokenbucket.go, autoscaler/core/policy_dispatch.go, controller/fleet_crd_v1alpha7.yaml, telemetry/metrics_burst.go, console/frontend/src/pages/dedicated/fleet/BurstTab.tsx, docs/dedicated/burst-controls.md, tests/autoscaler/burst_tokenbucket_test.go, perf-canary/playbooks/burst-sim.yaml.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement token-bucket autoscaling logic
- [x] Expose config in Fleet CRD and controller
- [x] Emit telemetry and console UI components
- [x] Add tests and perf canary
- [x] Docs and migration notes

Related: ENG-2145 (fleet autoscaling roadmap), PM-732 (burst controls requirements).

release_notes: Added a token-bucket burst autoscaling policy for Dedicated fleets (opt-in via autoscaler.burst.enable).
New CRD fields (v1alpha7) to configure max_burst_replicas, refill_rate_rps, token_cost_per_replica, and burst_cooldown.
New telemetry and console UI for tracking burst tokens and consumption.
Migration helper and docs included; default behavior unchanged.
notes: Performance impact: microbenchmarks show ~2% CPU increase in autoscaler loop under heavy evaluation; considered acceptable.
Operator guidance: enable autoscaler.burst.enable=false by default; recommended conservative refill_rate_rps for small fleets.
Follow-ups: telemetry retention policy change to keep burst metrics for 90 days for regression analysis (ENG-2980).
